title: "Edge security proposal"
description: "Disabled Cloudflare Pro fragments with origin-lock, authentication-limit and client-acceptance prerequisites."
---

This remains a draft proposal. Every generated rule is disabled. No DNS, rule,
setting, Worker, deployment or database change was applied. Finance and Finance
staging remain excluded. The independent review accepted documentation and
disabled fragments for integration, with the readiness requirements below. Steps 1–3 remain proposals for approval;
steps 4–5 are not ready for approval. Integration does not authorize infrastructure writes.

## Inventory and current limits

The [source inventory](/build/devops/edge-security-source) enumerates 1,824 app
entries across 30 apps, 461 legacy implementations and 1,375 client path literals.
These are source counts, not unique deployed endpoints. There are 563 explicitly
unknown generic auth classifications. The three source findings have separate
fix owners; this proposal changes none of those endpoints.

The [traffic evidence](/build/devops/edge-security-traffic) contains the original
24-hour Cloudflare query and separate bounded Vercel windows. Adaptive sampling,
pagination and timestamp-boundary limits remain explicit. Older counts are not
current deployment or caller-acceptance proof.

A fresh DNS read at **26 October 2026, 14:55 GMT+7** finds **31 of the original
36 application hosts DNS-only**, with five proxied. This corrects the review's
30/36 count. Adding `store.tuturuuu.com`, `stores.tuturuuu.com` and
`api.tuturuuu.com` produces **34 DNS-only out of 39**, still five proxied.
Cloudflare HTTP rules do nothing for their DNS-only traffic. The 39 names stay in
`candidateApplicationHosts`; only the five inventoried proxied app names are
active `applicationHosts` selectors. The validator rejects DNS-only or unknown
active hosts. Adding a name to
`policy.json` does not establish ownership, proxying or origin protection.
Custom domains such as `nova.ai.vn` and `rewise.me` need their own zone evidence.

`inventory/review-prerequisites.json` records the sanitized newer reads. At
**14:53 GMT+7**, normalization is `type=cloudflare`, `scope=both`. The custom
entrypoint is no longer empty: the Finance-owned TEMP skip is at position 1,
ID/ref `3543f90df80b4019a381dd34294dc3f5`. Its expression and parameters are
intentionally absent from the public packet. Preserve Finance custody and order.
Re-read immediately before any apply; the earlier empty snapshot is historical.

## Phase and plan capabilities

The observed plan is Pro Website. These are first-party documented capabilities,
not provider compilation or write-entitlement acceptance of these fragments.

| Construct | Supported scope and limit |
| --- | --- |
| Custom rules | Pro supports 20 rules without regex or the custom `log` action. Ordinary request headers are supported here. [Availability](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/custom-rules/), [header example](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/custom-rules/use-cases/require-specific-headers/). |
| Prefix expressions | Use the function `starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/api/auth/")`, not an infix operator. Normal path fields work in custom rules and Pro rate-limit expressions. [Function](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ruleset-engine/rules-language/functions/#starts_with). |
| Rate-limit fields | Pro permits host, URI/path/full URI/query and verified-bot filtering, with IP counters and at most two rules. Request headers, method and UA are not Pro rate-expression entitlements. IP counters do not grant IP/header filtering. [Plan matrix](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/rate-limiting-rules/#availability). |
| Rate-limit actions | Custom/rate `log` is Enterprise-only. The candidate uses `block` with JSON 429. The existing leaked-password rule consumes one of two slots and stays intact. [Actions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ruleset-engine/rules-language/actions/), [parameters](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/rate-limiting-rules/parameters/). |
| Transport skip | Only `products: ["bic", "securityLevel"]` and phase `http_request_sbfm` are skipped. Managed WAF, rate limiting and remaining custom rules stay active. Plain BFM cannot be skipped. [Options](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/custom-rules/skip/options/). |
| Header removal | `rewrite` in `http_request_late_transform`, with `headers.<name>.operation=remove`, removes the probe header after security matching and before origin delivery. [API shape](https://developers.cloudflare.com/rules/transform/request-header-modification/create-api/). |
| Configuration | `set_config` in `http_config_settings` accepts boolean `bic` and `security_level: "off"`. [Settings](https://developers.cloudflare.com/rules/configuration-rules/settings/). |

An SBFM-phase skip does **not establish a blanket "Block AI bots" exception**.
AI Crawl Control selections can be separate WAF custom rules and therefore are
not skipped by this proposal. The interaction with the current legacy/migrated
AI bot settings remains unverified. A bounded GET of the SBFM entrypoint returned
400 `unknown phase`; this is a read limitation, not evidence that SBFM is absent.
Resolve the specific admitted machine-path behavior before apply. Do not skip
all remaining custom rules to manufacture that acceptance.
[AI Crawl Control ordering](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-crawl-control/configuration/ai-crawl-control-with-waf/),
[AI policy behavior](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/additional-configurations/block-ai-bots/).

Labyrinth injection/crawl events are not block or challenge actions. No per-path
Labyrinth skip was established. Existing managed CF/OWASP definitions returned
block/log/score actions, with no enabled challenge action in the earlier read.
Vendor-managed log actions do not grant Pro custom/rate log support. Refresh
these definitions and their existing Meet exceptions before rollout.
[Labyrinth](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/additional-configurations/ai-labyrinth/).

## Normalization and origin lock are prerequisites

`policy.json` and its validator require `type=cloudflare`, `scope=both`, and a
fresh pre-apply read. Matching the same normalized URL at edge and origin avoids
an incoming/origin interpretation split. A type value alone does not establish
scope. Any normalization change affects the zone, including Finance; only the
zone owner can admit it. Test encoded unreserved characters, duplicate slashes,
dot segments and callback/signature URLs in bounded fixtures before promotion.
[Settings and scope](https://developers.cloudflare.com/rules/normalization/settings/).

**ORIGIN LOCK precedes browser enforcement and the new auth limit.** A caller
that can reach an origin alias directly can avoid every Cloudflare rule.

| Origin | Required future control | Acceptance and rollback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cloudflare Workers | Set both `workers_dev=false` and `preview_urls=false` in the authoritative publisher configuration and reconcile hosted production/version URLs. Coverage derives from `publishers.json`, joined to the canonical targets and actual publisher config. Include native Meet `apps/meet/void.config.ts:45`, Meet realtime, Lettin, Parley and Colab. Colab now explicitly sets both URL flags false in source; this is not a deployment. | Prove canonical host works and production/preview workers.dev URLs cannot bypass zone controls. Capture previous route/version settings. Roll back only the admitted Worker settings under its owner; stop enforcement while any bypass is reopened. |
| Existing Vercel origins | Vercel Firewall must deny unless the actual provider-observed source is in Cloudflare's published source ranges **and** an exact, separate edge-injected secret header is valid. Overwrite client-supplied `x-tuturuuu-edge-origin` at the authorized edge. Header presence or Cloudflare source IP alone is insufficient. | Establish current Vercel plan support and source-IP semantics; do not trust client X-Forwarded-For. Prove direct requests fail with no header, forged header and wrong secret, while authorized edge traffic succeeds. If this cannot be enforced, hold rollout. |
| Vercel aliases | Apply the origin restriction to every project deployment URL, including `<app>-tuturuuu.vercel.app`, branch aliases and immutable deployment URLs. Preserve approved deployment protection. Inventory direct internal/CI callbacks before restricting them. | Verify canonical host and aliases separately. Roll back the new project rule by captured ID/version, with browser/auth enforcement paused. Do not add a broad alias/IP/UA bypass to repair a probe. |
| DNS-only hosts | Separately authorize and prove proxy/canonical ingress plus header injection before enabling the origin restriction for that host. | A Cloudflare-only restriction on a still-DNS-only app would reject its callers. Restore that host's recorded ingress/origin rule together under the release owner, never change Finance from this lane. |

Workers.dev and version URLs are independent settings; changing only one does
not prove origin closure. No Worker config is edited or deployed by this PR.
These are temporary protections for existing origins during the Cloudflare
migration, not new runtime or scheduler dependencies.
[workers.dev](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/routing/workers-dev/),
[version URLs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/versions-and-deployments/version-urls/),
[Vercel WAF conditions](https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-firewall/vercel-waf/custom-rules),
[proxy limitations](https://vercel.com/kb/guide/can-i-use-a-proxy-on-top-of-my-vercel-deployment),
[Cloudflare source ranges](https://www.cloudflare.com/ips/).

## Traffic classes and the last Pro rate-limit slot

Machine classification is transport treatment, not authentication. `/api/*`
includes pre-auth OTP, password and CLI verify/refresh operations, public APIs,
cookie sessions and invalid-token canaries. Keep origin actor/tenant checks,
Turnstile, one-use capabilities, webhook signatures and replay controls intact.

The former Meet 6,000/60-second catch-all is removed. The remaining Pro slot is
reserved for **20 requests per 60 seconds per IP/colo** on currently proxied
app hosts and only `/api/v1/auth/`, `/api/auth/`, `/api/cli/auth/`. Its mitigation
is a 60-second block with JSON 429 (`AUTH_RATE_LIMITED`, `retryAfter: 60`).
This is a proposed low threshold, not calibrated NAT capacity. Counters can be
shared across matching hosts and paths for the same IP/colo. No method, header,
probe-secret exclusion or per-token edge counter is claimed on Pro. Exact
server-refresh and polling paths are excluded below; they retain application
authentication, token validity, quota and abuse controls. Preserve the
existing leaked-password rule. Expand the host list only after origin/proxy
acceptance, shared-NAT measurement and client 429 acceptance. Per-token and
per-IP quotas after origin authentication remain application responsibilities.
Any future Cloudflare limiter must bound work/retries, preserve idempotent
progress and terminal states, and prove a durable stop fence before rollout.

| Class | Treatment |
| --- | --- |
| Browser pages and forms | Keep BIC/managed WAF and existing server-verified Turnstile. `edge_browser_bic` is a **no-op while zone BIC is on**; it adds no new browser protection. Stronger zone-wide bot controls require Finance-safe admission. |
| Machine APIs | Narrow BIC/SBFM/Security Level skips, with origin auth and the auth limit retained. `security_level: off` and skipping `securityLevel` explicitly opt these paths out of **Under Attack** checks too. This availability/security tradeoff requires origin lock and application abuse controls; toggling zone Under Attack will not protect exempt APIs. |
| Static assets | Only `/_next/static/` gets the generic Next transport exemption. `/_next/image` is billable and stays protected. No `/_next/data/` exception is currently justified; add a host-specific data path only with an actual caller trace. |
| Auth redirects | `/auth/login` and `/auth/callback` are machine redirects on **Colab only**. Other hosts' auth pages keep browser protection. |
| Hive socket | Source maps the public socket to `hive.tuturuuu.com/realtime`, with signed query token and internal `hive-realtime:7815`. Only that exact public path is exempted. Hive pages remain browser traffic. A live 101/invalid-token 401 is still required. |
| Webhooks | Preserve raw-body signature/shared-secret and dedupe checks. Published Square/Polar CIDRs remain observation-only in `webhook-origins.json`; no IP/ASN/UA authentication bypass. |
| Own probes | Narrow read method, host/path and rotating low-value secret; no UA/IP-only identity. The header is removed before origin, without changing origin auth or the invalid-key 401 canary. |

Hive evidence: `docker-compose/compose.web.prod.sidecars.yml:26`,
`scripts/docker-web/blue-green.js:1510`,
`apps/hive/src/app/api/v1/hive/servers/[serverId]/realtime-token/route.ts:59`,
`packages/hive-ui/src/realtime/hive-realtime-client.ts:41`.
The Compose/proxy material is retained source, not a claim that the paused Docker
runtime was started or that current deployment/handshake acceptance was observed.

It does not confuse a source publication hold with absence of an existing Worker.

Other publisher/runtime configurations remain unchanged.

## Shared refresh and polling must not use the login-attempt counter

Server app-session maintenance calls its **own public request origin** through
`getAuthApiUrl` (`packages/auth/src/proxy/index.ts:229`). Verification at `:316`
and signed refresh at `:455`/`signed-refresh.ts:124` send cookie + JSON without an
edge identity header. Many users can share a server egress-IP counter. Refresh
429 can become invalid refresh credentials when no still-valid access remains
(`packages/auth/src/proxy/signed-refresh.ts:135`). Do not interpret that as a bad
user token or roll out a limit that causes mass session failure.

The generated strict auth-attempt expression excludes these exact paths:

- `/api/auth/refresh-app-session` and `/api/auth/verify-app-token`.
- Central second hops `/api/v1/auth/cross-app-session/refresh` and
  `/api/v1/auth/cross-app-token/verify`.
- MFA pending reads `/api/v1/auth/mfa/mobile/approvals`.
- The capability-bearing QR challenge subtree
  `/api/v1/auth/qr-login/challenges/`, including polling and approval. The challenge
  creation endpoint without the trailing segment remains in the attempt counter.

These transport/counter exclusions confer no origin authorization. Keep token,
cookie, signed refresh, replay and application abuse controls. The exclusion is
necessary until a separate design distinguishes valid server work from attempts;
never identify it by UA, IP or header presence alone. Before **step 5**, verify
this compiled exclusion or provide a controlled trace proving the specific
subrequest does not enter the counter. The current source is not such a trace.

QR polls every **2 seconds**, roughly 30/minute/device plus the initial read
(`qr_login_sign_in_page.dart:30`, `:106`, `:121`). MFA approvals poll every
**5 seconds**, roughly 12/minute/device plus event-triggered reads
(`mfa_approval_listener.dart:18`, `:47`, `:104`). Both use `/api/v1/auth/` on the
apex by default. QR 429 becomes a terminal error; MFA drops retryAfter and
continues polling. Do not add `tuturuuu.com` to the strict auth limit until these
reads are excluded or reshaped and accepted. One-second MFA UI timers are not
one-second HTTP polling.

Before step 5, calibrate the proposed threshold against **measured per-IP p99**
on each proxied host, including peak authentication bursts, server egress sharing,
multiple devices and Vietnamese mobile CGNAT. Record measurement window, sample
coverage and accepted caller failures; the historical aggregate snapshots do not
provide that p99. The validator requires inventoried application hosts and a
proxied DNS row for every rate-limit host; DNS-only apex cannot be added silently.

## Client 429 acceptance is still required

These are source traces, not executed Dart/CLI acceptance. No client is changed
in this proposal. Do not enable the aggressive auth rule until owners prove
bounded error/cooldown handling, no unintended logout and no one-use-token or
unknown-write replay under JSON and HTML 429 responses.

| Client | Observed behavior and limit | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dart JSON API | Safely parses JSON or HTML errors, preserves 429, and parses numeric/HTTP-date Retry-After with JSON retryAfter fallback. General requests do not retry 429 automatically. | `apps/mobile/lib/data/sources/api_client.dart:609`, `:638`, `:662`, `:521` |
| Mobile auth | OTP-send preserves cooldown and disables resend. OTP-verify drops retryAfter; password repository preserves it but cubit drops it. Some OTP cooldown text can be hidden without a retained duration. | `apps/mobile/lib/data/repositories/auth_repository.dart:166`, `:201`, `:272`; `apps/mobile/lib/features/auth/cubit/auth_cubit.dart:190`, `:230`; `apps/mobile/lib/features/auth/view/login_page.dart:148`, `:281` |
| CLI verify/refresh | Non-2xx throws a status-only error before parsing JSON; Retry-After is ignored and there is no 429 backoff. | `packages/sdk/src/cli/auth.ts:65`, `:98`; `packages/sdk/src/cli/index.ts:29` |
| Server satellite refresh | Self-origin verify/refresh can share an egress IP across users. Non-403/503 refresh errors including 429 may invalidate continuation. The exact maintenance paths are excluded from the strict attempt counter; controlled acceptance is still required. | `packages/auth/src/proxy/index.ts:229`, `:316`, `:455`; `packages/auth/src/proxy/signed-refresh.ts:124`, `:135` |
| Mobile recurring reads | QR 2-second polling stops as an error on 429; MFA 5-second polling drops retryAfter and keeps polling. Both need exclusions or redesign before strict apex enforcement. | `apps/mobile/lib/features/security/qr_login/view/qr_login_sign_in_page.dart:30`; `apps/mobile/lib/features/security/mfa_approval/view/mfa_approval_listener.dart:18`, `:104` |
| User SDK/internal API | Refresh retry handles 401, not 429. Error transport preserves message/code but not a retryAfter property. | `packages/sdk/src/platform.ts:950`; `packages/internal-api/src/internal-api-error.ts:29` |
| Storage SDK | Handles JSON/HTML 429 and numeric Retry-After. Optional bounded retries cap delay at 30 seconds, shorter than the proposed 60-second mitigation; some methods do not retry. | `packages/sdk/src/storage.ts:924`, `:1002`, `:1028` |
| EPM SDK | JSON 429 loses retry headers; HTML 429 becomes NetworkError. No backoff loop is shown. | `packages/sdk/src/epm.ts:565`, `:584` |

The JSON body supports Dart's existing fallback. Do not assume a custom edge
response also supplies Retry-After; capture the actual header/body in acceptance.
Do not automatically replay OTP/CLI exchange or mutations merely because a retry
window elapsed. Preserve the original operation/capability and reconcile outcomes.

## Probe disclosure, removal and rotation

The probe credential is **plaintext inside the rule expression** and readable
by any token with ruleset-read access. It is not an application credential or
proof of a trusted actor. Use an independent, low-value, short-lived value for
this narrow transport exemption. Never reuse it for origin lock, bearer auth,
webhooks, deployment protection or a broader WAF bypass. Keep reader access least
privilege and exclude raw probe values from logs and public artifacts.

`late-transform.json` removes every `x-tuturuuu-edge-probe` header value on
admitted non-Finance hosts, including values that failed the probe predicate.
Security matching runs before this late phase. The removal prevents forwarding
the credential to origin; it does not hide values from Cloudflare/ruleset readers.
Origin authorization and other headers remain unchanged.

Rotation uses at most two accepted values and a **10-minute overlap**:

1. Provision B privately. Keep A valid while the admitted rule accepts A or B.
   Leave the late removal rule active. Capture rule IDs/versions and redacted
   fingerprints, not the values.
2. Switch admitted probes to B and verify matched/unmatched probes plus origin
   header absence with controlled evidence. Preserve invalid-origin-key 401.
3. Once all admitted callers acknowledge B, remove A within the overlap deadline.
   If callers cannot switch by the deadline, roll back to A-only and restore their
   prior configuration rather than extend dual acceptance indefinitely.
4. Revoke A and verify it no longer qualifies. On compromise, revoke the affected
   value immediately; do not preserve it for convenience. Rollback must never
   restore a compromised value. If both values are suspect, disable only the probe
   exemption while preserving header removal and origin/application controls.

No real value or automatic rotation controller is introduced by this PR.

## High-value origin-secret handling

The origin-lock value bypasses the entire Cloudflare front door at a Vercel
origin when combined with an accepted Cloudflare source. It is **high value**,
separate from the low-value probe secret. `origin-transform.json` uses a disabled
`set` operation that overwrites client input. Its eligible hosts are derived from
verified Vercel bindings plus proxied DNS, excluding Worker and Finance hosts.
No non-Finance proxied Vercel origin is currently verified in this packet, so
its expression is `false`. Do not broaden it to every proxied satellite.

Static values in Cloudflare Transform Rules are readable to ruleset-read token
holders. Vercel Developer/Viewer roles can view WAF rules; the configuration-read
API includes condition values. Treat the embedded condition as readable by that
configuration-reader trust boundary, even if one UI masks it. Step-4 evidence
must identify the actual people, groups, service identities and tokens that can
read **each side**, their permissions and the owner's explicit acceptance. Keep
private identity evidence outside Git. Restrict both provider readers to least
privilege; revoke unused access. Role documentation alone is not an account audit.
[CF configuration readers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ruleset-engine/rulesets-api/view/#view-a-specific-ruleset),
[Vercel roles](https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-firewall/vercel-waf/custom-rules#access-roles),
[condition-read response](https://vercel.com/docs/rest-api/security/read-firewall-configuration).

Rotate a high-entropy origin value in this order, preserving the Cloudflare-source
requirement throughout: **Vercel accepts A and B → Cloudflare sets B → Vercel
removes A**. Verify positive canonical traffic and negative direct/no/wrong-header
cases between steps. Use a bounded owner-recorded overlap and acknowledgments;
never log the values or store them in the repository. Normal rollback can return
to A only while A remains trusted, with the matching Vercel acceptance retained.

On compromise, remove the affected value from Vercel immediately, revoke leaked
reader credentials, provision a fresh value through trusted access and switch the
edge. If no trusted value/path remains, isolate or fail closed at the origin and
invoke the release owner's recovery; never temporarily allow arbitrary headers,
all Cloudflare IPs alone, or a compromised value to restore availability. Record
all rule IDs/versions and reconcile unknown writes before retry. None is applied here.

## Rollout, ordering and rollback

Every future apply captures the exact source, fresh phase/version, before/after
rule IDs, refs, relative positions, actions and owner. Re-read the custom entrypoint
**immediately before applying**, preserve the Finance-owned TEMP rule and obtain
its owner's coordination. Insert owned skip rules **before terminating custom
block/challenge rules** without skipping remaining custom rules. Cross-phase
order is provider-defined; the auth rate limit remains active after custom skips.
Never replace an entrypoint with this fragment's whole rule array.

| Order | Admission and acceptance | Rollback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Resolve source gaps | Separate fix owners handle External, Playground and legacy Supermemory. Review other auth/signature and host-binding gaps. | No infrastructure change; preserve open blockers. |
| 2. Read and prove readiness | Re-read normalization cloudflare/both, DNS, quotas, all relevant phases and Finance custody. Capture IDs/positions. Resolve AI-policy coverage and controlled client 429 behavior. | Stop before apply if any fact or caller behavior is unknown. |
| 3. Prepare disabled fragments/probes | Under fresh admission, add only owned disabled fragments, header removal and private A/B rotation configuration in safe order. Establish caller updates and origin header absence before enabling the probe exemption. | Remove/disable only newly owned rules by captured ID; preserve foreign rules and origin auth. |
| 4. ORIGIN LOCK | Fresh GET every Worker, resolve legacy/rollback aliases and actual rule-reader identities first. Per host, separately admit proxy/canonical ingress, edge-origin header injection, Vercel Firewall/alias protection or workers.dev/version URL closure. Prove positive canonical traffic and negative direct-origin cases. | Restore that host's recorded origin/ingress controls with enforcement stopped. Do not restore a compromised secret. Finance remains separately owned. |
| 5. Auth limit and transport canary | After origin lock, server/poll exclusions, client 429 and measured per-IP p99/CGNAT acceptance, admit the low auth rule with the matching machine transport exceptions on one host. Place skips before custom block/challenge rules. No interstitials for API/socket traffic. | Disable the new auth rule and owned transport/config rules by ID. Retain leaked-password protection, app auth and header removal. |
| 6. Browser enforcement | Preserve the BIC baseline. Admit stronger bot controls only after all machine/control/object paths and specific AI policy behavior are proven and Finance releases its hold. | Restore only captured bot/config values under the zone owner. Record any Under Attack exception that remains. |
| 7. Provider IP filters and expansion | Re-read published environment CIDRs, prove signatures/dedupe, then admit one host/provider at a time. DNS-only and custom domains require separate origin/zone acceptance. | Revert only the new IP/host restriction; retain signature checks, dedupe and prior safe rules. |
| 8. App-owned header end state | Follow the [header matrix and staged plan](/build/devops/edge-security-headers). Prove every affected app/runtime first, then separately authorize Managed Transform Add security headers OFF. Finance scoped exceptions stay separately owned. | Restore captured transform/exception state if unexplained policy loss occurs, with each app owner involved. No global change in this PR. |

Any valid-caller challenge, incorrect 401/429, one-use-token loss, stalled stream
or socket, or direct-origin success stops expansion. Reconcile unknown provider
writes before retry. No provider writes, new runtime/datastore, deployment,
production SSH, M4 build or source-lead fix is part of this amendment.

The [framing inventory](/build/devops/edge-security-headers) records the new
Managed Transform finding and separates current root headers from intended
application policy and unverified embed behavior.

## Verification and review disposition

`policy.json` compiles into seven disabled rules in `custom.json`,
`configuration.json`, `rate-limit.json`, `late-transform.json` and
`origin-transform.json`. The origin-secret set fragment is also nonmatching
(`false`) until a proxied Vercel origin is independently verified.

```sh
node scripts/edge-security-rules.mjs --write
node scripts/edge-security-rules.mjs
node --test scripts/edge-security-rules.test.mjs
```

The local validator rejects missing origin/normalization/custody prerequisites,
broad Next/auth scopes, aggressive-limit drift, missing header removal, more than
two probe values, Finance scope and compiled JSON drift. This does not establish
provider compilation, live origin lock or executed Dart/CLI acceptance.

| Review item | Disposition before apply |
| --- | --- |
| P1 origin bypass | Required origin-lock step, Worker/alias controls and rollback encoded; actual closure still unexecuted. |
| P2 pre-auth APIs | Last Pro slot reserved for low auth-path limit; 429 source gaps explicitly hold enforcement. |
| P2 probe secret | Plaintext-reader risk, low-value A/B overlap and late header removal encoded. |
| P2 normalization | cloudflare/both and re-read required by policy/validator; observed both at 14:53 GMT+7. |
| P3 path scopes/aliases | Static-only Next paths, Colab-only redirects, store/stores/api aliases and Hive exact socket path encoded. |
